transcript: The other night, Paul and I saw Cats: The Jellicle Ball at the Perelman Performing Arts Center in FiDi and it was literally everything I hoped for and more. Now, Cats is a very divisive piece — I happen to be someone who actually loves it, so I went in wanting to enjoy this production, but I do think that gave me high expectations. To my utter delight, this production was spectacular, easily one of my favorite theater pieces I've seen so far this year. The musical is basically series of songs, most of which each introduce a specific cat. It's a big ensemble piece, a big dance show, and you could say less plot driven. In this reimagined production through the lens of ballroom culture, the songs are the backdrop for a series of runways with various CATegories. The score and the lyrics are pretty much unchanged, but otherwise this is a very sharp departure from classic productions. There are clubier orchestrations and design elements, a literal catwalk as the stage, fabulously opulent costumes, and overall really creative choices. This production is so celebratory, unapologetically queer, and honestly just a big party — everyone in the audience was loving it. I know I'm biased being a queer person who loves Cats, but I really cannot recommend this production enough. It's so creative, so well done, the directorial choices and overall concept is so smart, and the performances eat. So happy pride month to us. With that, another program for my collection.
